: This X-AP will be executed when the player clicks the TEMPL button.
You specify which of these macros will be used in the "Scenario Data" screen. For more info on the "Scenario Data" screen see the chapter "Scenario Startup Information"
Quests
Quests is just a snappy name I give to a set of flags you can use to keep track of events that have happened in the scenario.
There are 100 Quests that can be either TRUE or FALSE to show if that Quest has been completed or not. They all start in the FALSE position.
If you want to keep track of events that have happened, you can assign a Quest flag to each event and set it to TRUE when the event has been completed.
Example: Lets say you have 3 major battles you want to take place prior to letting the party get into a castle.
Assume that Quest ID 1 represents the first battle:
Assume that Quest ID 2 represents the second battle:
Assume that Quest ID 3 represents the third battle:
In the script that follows each battle you would have a code 47 (Set/Clear Quest) after the battle. If the party is victorious in battle no. 1 then you would set Quest ID 1 to TRUE to show that they have completed that particular quest.
The same holds true for Quest 2 and Quest 3. At the end of each battle you would set the Quest that represents that battle to TRUE.
At the entrance to the castle you would have a script that checks to see if each of Quest 1, 2 and 3 are TRUE. If all are TRUE then you would proceed to let them in the castle.
You would need to use a series of three Code 46s to check for each Quest flag in turn. If all 3 are set you can have it continue the script and let them in the castle.
You can use Quests to keep track of lever positions, battles won, areas explored, items taken or just about anything that can be either TRUE or FALSE.
Variable Quest Flags
Even though most quests can be treated as just a TRUE or FALSE to depict whether or not the party has completed a set task, you can also use these quest flags to keep track of variables.
Each quest flag can have a value from -127 through 127.
You can add or subtract to each of these quests using a code 76 and have the game automaticaly branch when the quest flag reaches a certain value.
Example
: You could have a large number of battles, each of which are assigned a point value from 1 to 3.
At the end of each battle you could run a script that increments quest flag number 1 by the value of 1-3 depending on how tough that particular battle was.
Then you can check at any time to see if quest flag number 1 is more than 20. If at any time it become 20 or more you could have it branch to an action point where you award the party a set treaure or any other type of reward.
This is just one example and is a pretty simple one at that. You can use these quest flags to keep track of all kinds of info and then test it at any time with a code 77

sections.title: Monster Mash
sections.text:
23. Monster Mash
Top
Monster Mash
OK. So you want to use some monster icons that are not in the standard set available but are in the Monster Mash. To import the icons from Monster Mash to your scenario file is a pretty simple process. If you want to add icons to the Monster Mash so you can use them in future scenarios, see the section, "Adding Monster And Item Icons"
Realmz is only capable of holding around 127 sets of monster icons for any one scenario. Realmz has a standard set that is used by default. You can override these default icons by telling your scenario which ones to use in place of the default icons. To access the area where you do this, select "Build Icon Set" from the Monster Editor as shown below.
Figure 16.0
Figure 16.1
The default set as usable by the scenario is displayed on the left side and those monsters contained in the Monster Mash are shown on the right side. To import icons from Monster Mash just click and drag on the icon you want and release it over the icon on the left you want to be overridden.
In the example above, Icon #409 from Monster Mash is being substituted for Icon #387 of the standard set. Whenever icon #387 is used, it will instead be the tall spear toting giant you wanted instead of the tiny goblin as was the default.
Note
: a small document symbol
appears to the right of any icons that have been imported. This makes it easy for you to tell which icons are imported and are overriding a standard icon.
It's that simple. To remove the new icon and restore the default, then just click and drag back to the right.
You can also achieve this by placing the correct IDs and selecting the correct buttons from the top of the screen, but the click & drag method is much easier.

sections.title: Vault of Arcana
sections.text:
24. Vault of Arcana
Top
Vault of Arcana
When you create your own items for use with your scenario you need to select an icon to represent it. If the standard icons don't have what you are looking for, then perhaps you will find something in the Vault of Arcana.
The Vault is just a collection of miscellaneous icons. If you want to add one of them to your scenario file then click the "Edit Icon Set" button from the treasure editor as shown in Figure 17.0.
Figure 17.0
Figure 17.1
This is an example of some of the special icons that were used in "Destroy the Necronomicon" If you wanted to import a new icon from the Vault of Arcana into this scenario, you would just Click & Drag the icon from the right side to the position on the left side you wanted it to occupy. This works almost exactly like the Monster Mash editor.
A small scroll symbol in the left hand column shows that the icon is currently a part of your scenario file.

sections.title: Adding Monster & Item Icons
sections.text:
25. Adding Monster & Item Icons
Top
Adding Monster and Item Icons
To add new icons to Monster Mash or Vault of Arcana you must use ResEdit in a similar fashion as with adding special land tiles.
If you open either Monster Mash or Vault of Arcana using ResEdit you will find many color icons already there. If you add new icons remember to follow these guidelines.
1) Always make the icons Purgeable . Select 'Get Information' on any icon and it will bring up a window like the one in Figure 18.0.
Figure 18.0
As in the above example, the Purgeable attribute is set. All icons used in your scenario should have the same attributes as those shown above.
To add a new icon for use in Vault of Arcana, set the ID: of the icon to anything in a range from 30126 to 32000.
To add a new icon for use in Monster Mash you need to have a set of two icons. One for the creature facing left and another for the creature facing right.
For the left facing icon it must be in a range of 518 to 600. The right facing icons must = the same ID No. + 308. So if your left facing icon is 550, your right facing icon would have to be 858.

sections.title: Creating Special Land Tiles
sections.text:
26. Creating Special Land Tiles
Top
Creating Special Land Tiles
So you want to use some special graphics of your own design in Realmz as land tiles. To add a special land tile you will need to use ResEdit. If you're not familiar with ResEdit then you may want to breeze through the ResEdit manual prior to using it. ResEdit is very powerful and you can easily mess up your files if you are not careful. ALWAYS make a backup of any files you are about to open with ResEdit as once you have made a mistake, you may not be able to correct it.
Once you have your special land tile created using some drawing program, (32x32 Pixels in size) you are ready to add it to your scenario.
Inside your scenario folder is a file by the title "Scenario". From within ResEdit open that file. You should see something like Figure 19.0
Figure 19.0
Double click on the 'cicn' to Open the Icon Resources. You should see something like figure 19.1
We have already created about 35 blank icons ready to be used. To paste in your graphic for you new land tile, double click on the -100 icon. That will open the ICON editor and you should see something like figure 19.2
Figure 19.1
Figure 19.2
From here you can just paste in your graphic and even use the simple tools that ResEdit provides. After you have done so, you can simply close all the above windows. The next time you run Divinity, you will notice that land tile No. -100 will now look like your brand new graphic.
Note
: If your special tile does not cover the entire 32x32 area provided, you can make a mask. To do so, click on the small WYSIWYG version of the icon (Point 1) on the upper right of the window and DRAG it to the MASK region (Point 2). This will create a mask. When the icon is plotted on the game map, only those sections that have a corresponding black pixel in the mask will be drawn. The remainder of the white area will be drawn with the default grass or dirt of the type of land used.
Don't bother with the Black and White portions of the Icons or Mask as they are not used in any way. Adding the B&W portion will only cause your data files to be larger than necessary.
It's that easy. A word of warning. These tiles draw much slower than the standard land tiles. If you place a large block of custom tiles on your map in any one area, it will really slow the game down. Divinity has to draw these in a different way that is much slower than the standard terrain tiles.

sections.title: Adding Pictures & Sounds To Your Scenario
sections.text:
27. Adding Pictures & Sounds To Your Scenario
Top
Adding Pictures To Your Scenario
You fancy yourself an artist and you want to place some of your own artwork in the game. Using a Code 27 you can display a picture in the display. But how do you get those pictures into the scenario data files you ask?
Click the button "Scenario Data" from the Land Editor. A button labeled "Picture Editor" is in the upper left hand corner of the screen that appears.
Figure 20.0
When you click "Picture Editor" it will bring up the screen where you can add and remove pictures for your scenario.
You use ID numbers to identify the individual pictures for display in the game. This screen will let you find a blank slot and to paste a picture from the clipboard into your scenario files.
Valid IDs range from 32000 to 30128. Note, however, that 32128 is the default ID that should be used for the splash screen of your scenario. Picture ID 32128 will be displayed each time the player loads a saved game.
Figure 20.1
Above is a small view of the screen used to edit the pictures in your scenario. The - + buttons will move from one slot to the next. Any pictures already in your files under the selected ID will be displayed.
Delete Current Picture
will remove the current picture from the scenario files. Note: This removes it for good. It does NOT send it to the clipboard.
Paste From Clipboard
will paste into the current ID the picture stored in your computers clipboard. Just copy your art from your paint program or scrapbook and click this button to place it into your scenario files.
Previous Stored Picture
and
Next Stored Picture
will advance the ID counter to the next picture in the current scenario file. It will skip all unused slots until it finds a stored picture and display that picture.
All pictures will be displayed centered in a 320 pixel x 320 pixel screen. If your picture is larger than that you should trim it down. If it's smaller it will be displayed centered in the 320x320 window.
Adding Sounds To Your Scenario
I have a tin ear myself, but if you have some actual talent and want to add a few custom sounds to your scenario then here is how you go about it.
1) Create your sounds. They need to be in a System Sound format. As an example, if the sound file is sitting on your hard drive, and you double click it, and it plays. Then it's in the right format.
Here is an example of what a valid sound file looks like.
2) Open up your sound file using ResEdit. When you do, you should see a window like this:
Double Click on the snd resource
to bring up a list of sounds in the file.
Figure 20.2
When you open up the snd resource you should see something like this:
Figure 20.3
The name, Size and ID of your sound will be different but the idea is the same.
Select "Get Info" from the "Resource" menu to bring up the following window.
Figure 20.4
If it is not already, click the "Purgeable" check box as that needs to be set to ON.
Change the ID of the sound to anything from 200 to 500. This is so it will not conflict with any sounds already used in the game.
Close the INFO window to bring up the same window as Figure 20.3
Copy your sound to the clipboard by choosing "Copy" from the Edit menu.
You can now close your sound file.
3) Open up the file titled "Scenario" that is inside your scenario folder using ResEdit.
Choose "Paste" from the Edit menu to paste your sound from the clipboard into the Scenario file. Then close and save the scenario file.
You can now have your scenario play your new sound by sending the ID of the sound you just created just like any other sound.

sections.title: Standard Land Tile Editor
sections.text:
28. Standard Land Tile Editor
Top
Standard Land Tile Editor
Starting in version 1.0.5 of Divinity you can now create your own land tile sets. The following information will give you all the info you need to know to either tweak an existing tile set to fit your needs -OR- design a whole new set all your own.
To get to the Land Tile Editor you will see a new button on the Land Editor with the title "Graphics" That button will take you to the screen show below. From here you can create custom tile sets you can distribute with your scenario.
Before I get into the long and short of how to go about doing this I would like to mention a few very important things.
1)
The size of these tile sets is in the area of 200k. Even if you use a standard tile set and want to make the slightest of changes, it will increase your scenario file size by 200k. Keep this in mind.
2)
Two tiles in particular for every land set can't be touched. That is the solid water and the sold mountain tiles. ID = 60 and ID = 61 I won't go into why, but those two tiles must be the same for each tile set and must be in the same place as well.
Current limitations:
At present each tile set can only have 200 tiles. Only one tile set can be loaded in memory at one time during game play. This is why every tile on any one land level must all come from a single tile set.
Tile 1
Tile 20
Tile 200
In Lower Right Corner
Looking at the editor screen you will see the entire land tile set currently loaded in the top 3/4 of the screen. Each 32x32 block is a single land tile and has an ID to depict its place. Tile 1 is in the very upper left, Tile 20 is in the very upper right and tile 200 is in the very lower right.
Just like reading words on a page, from left to right, top to bottom they are numbered..... 1 2 3 etc.
This one tile set will be used for all land level design as well as the majority of the tiles used for creating combat maps. More info on how the Combat Maps are created will be covered later.
Each tile has a number of attributes that tell the game how to treat it. As an example, Tile 130 (Horizontal Bridge) is currently selected.
List of Tile Attributes
Sound
Time/Move
Solid
Shore
Is / Need Boat
Is Path
Blocks Line of Sight
Need Fly / Float
Forest Type
The light blue section in the lower right of the editor contains all the fields for tile attributes.
Sound:
The Sound ID to play when the party walks over the tile. These range from 82 to 90. Many sound similar and what sound you pick really does not matter all that much. Just pick a sound you think sounds right for the type of terrain your making.
If you want to create any special sounds to play on particular land tiles, you can add them as ID 91 through 127 using ResEdit to the file "Scenario" inside your scenario folder.
Time/Move:
This tells the game how long it takes to walk over a certain land tile as well as how many movement points it will take to walk over this tile in combat.
When the tile is used for a land level the TIME value is multiplied by 5 minutes to get the amount of time it takes to cross. The Bridge takes 2 time units or 2 x 5 = 10 minutes of game time to cross.
This is important as the check for random encounters from Random Rectangles takes place every 5 minutes of game time. The higher this value, the longer it takes to cross this tile in game time.
When the tile is used in combat, this value is the number of movement points it takes to walk onto in combat.
Now for a curve ball. If you notice the center bottom the screen you will see a 3 x 3 grid of tiles. This section is where you tell Divinity how to build a land tile for combat. In this case, it would expand the bridge tile (130) into the 3 x 3 section of land tiles shown. The Time/Move values of each piece as directed by this 3 x 3 grid is actually used in combat. In most cases, the tiles used to create the expanded combat map will be the same or have similar attributes to the original tile but not always. (As in this case)
Solid:
This one sets the ability for the party to move across the tile. In general, mountain, open sea, wall tiles etc. are not traversable by a party on foot and should be set to solid.
Shore:
This attribute is for any tile that can be reached by boat and will allow the party a place to get off the boat. In general only shoreline and islands should have this attribute.
Is / Need Boat:
This field can have one of 3 values.
0 = This tile is not a boat tile nor does it require a boat to traverse.
1 = This tile is a boat. If you design your own boats, set any boat tiles to 1. This tells the game to let the party get on or off it as if it were a boat.
2 = This tile requires a boat to cross. In general only open see (Tile 60) require a boat to traverse in the standard map sets.
Is Path:
Any tile that is set as Is Path will have a red cross placed on them
when the party walks over it to show they have traveled over it.
In addition, these tiles should be build using clear or traversable tiles for combat as they are used to keep area of the combat map from isolating creatures. If a battle takes place near a mountain side it's possible creatures may get placed on the far side of the mountain during combat setup. Paths allow you to place tunnels or paths between isolated areas to allow the party and monsters to reach each other in combat.
Blocks Line of Sight:
If the tile would block your line of site set this to 1. In the past the only Line of Sight was for the indoor castle tile set. Land Levels will now be able to use Line of Sight as well if you so desire. If you set a land level to use Line of Sight then all tiles that have this attribute will block line of site.
Needs Fly / Float:
This is a new feature incorporated into the new Tile System. Currently none of the standard tile sets use this feature. Any tiles that require Fly / Float can only be crossed when the party is either flying or levitating. You could use this to make some sort of lava barrier, chasm, magic ward on the floor of a dungeon that prevents walking across it etc.
Forest Type:
Here is one area that may still have some limitations when it comes to the control you have. As you know from combat, there are lots of trees and huge mushrooms that take the place of trees for the combat map. However, these tiles don't appear in the standard tile sets. That's because they reside in special tile sets. These tile sets are loaded in addition to the standard tile set during combat and contain the TREE icons and a few other special icons.
For now any tile with a Forest Type will get the correct form of trees or mushrooms placed on the map during combat. How these icons look and behave is currently out of your hands until I design a better way that is compatible with the current data files you have no control over the large tree tiles.
As can be seen in the above example, tiles 143 through 154 are forest tiles. In this case, each of these tiles has a Forest Type of 1. This sets them to normal trees and when the combat map is created large normal trees will be placed appropriately.
To help remind you off what some special values usable in this and the Is / Need Boat fields, a popup menu can be used for quick reference. It is located just to the left of the tile attribute fields.
Forest Type Values
0 = Not a forest tile
1 = Normal Trees
2 = Desert Trees
3 = Mushroom Grove
Indoor Tile Set:
If the area is an indoor area such as castle or fortress, check this box. This sets the time scale as the party wanders around. When outdoors the base scale is 5 minute and indoors is 1 minute.
Combat Map Tiles
When combat happens, the section of map around the party is expanded to 9 times normal size. Each land tile has a 3x3 grid of tiles that determines how it will look on the expanded combat map.
Here is an example of how one of the
angled mountain sections will be
built during combat.
Another example of how one section
of stream will look when contructed
for combat.
OK Now that you know a bit more about how the maps are created for combat, lets look at the tools you have to push all this data around.
Lets talk a look at the lower left section of the Tile Editor. This pretty much contains everything you need to move, edit and save the land tiles.
First lets talk about how you can design how your tile will look in combat when it is expaned to 9x normal size.
To fill in the 3x3 combat map grid Shift-Click on the tile you want to construct. You will notice that the "Build" check box is activated. You can now click on any tile in the tile map above and then on one of the 3x3 grid squares to change that grid square. When you have completed all 9 grid tiles you can either Shift-Click a different tile to construct that one or check OFF the Build check box.
Note
: To change any information concerning a tile such as sound, time, solid ect... can only be changed when the Build check box is ON.
I will describe what each of the other buttons and fields is for and how it works.
Copy
If you have a land tile that shares many traits with many other tiles you can quickly make copies of those statistices to other tiles. Select the tile that has the stats you want to copy to other tiles, then click Copy and then click on each tile you want to copy those traits to. When you are done, click OFF on Copy.
Base Tile
is used to specify the standard open land tile. This tile should be the most basic clear land tile such as grass or sand. This is the tile that will be placed underneath special tiles during gameplay so it is important to pick a plain jane tile for your base tile.
Erase Tile
If this check box is ON and you click and drag a tile from one location to another, the original tile is erased. Otherwise a copy of the tile is placed in the new location without removing the old tile.
First the most basic of operations, loading and saving the tile sets. In the lower left hand corner you will see "
Load Tile Map
" and "
Save Tiles As
". When you launch the Tile Editor will default to Plains. To load a different tile set to edit just click on the tile set name, (Click on the word Plains to the right of the Load Tile Map button) and it will advance to the next tile set. When you see the name of the set you want to work with, click "Load Tile Map"
If at any time you want to revert back to the last saved version of the map you are working on, just click the "
Load Tile Map
" button again to reload all the data as it was when it was last saved.
The "
Save Tiles As
" button will save the current Tile Set under the appropriate name. The standard tile sets can be loaded but not saved to. You can only save to "Custom 1" through "Custom 3"
To advance the "
Save Tiles As
" file click on the name of the file itself, (In this example, click on the word "Plains" to the right of the "
Save Tiles As
" button.)
Building Combat Expansion Model for Each Tile:
As was explained earlier, each tile must have a 3 x 3 grid of tiles to depict how it will look when expanded for the combat map.
Picture Import Bounds and Import Picture:
You have all kinds of cool art you want to use for land tiles. This little area is where you can import that art to the tile editor and get it set for placement above.
First off, all land tiles are 32x32 but you can design them as a block of tiles in another program and bring them in as one chunk. Here is a step by step process of getting a picture from your clipboard into the tile editor.
1) Create your tiles in your graphics program of choice. Make sure you use the System Palette as that is what Realmz uses.
2) Copy your artwork into the clipboard.
3) Open up the "Picture Editor" screen. For more info about how to do that, see the previous chapter, "Adding Pictures & Sounds To Your Scenario"
4) Paste your picture into your scenario file and remember the ID. This is only temporary as you will eventually delete it again.
5) Return back to the Tile Editor and place the ID of your picture you pasted into your scenario file in the small field just below the words Import Picture and to the right of the +/- buttons. If you have a number of pictures you will be importing one after the other, you can scan through them using the +/- buttons.
6) Place into the Height and Width fields the size of your picture. They must be in increments of 32 x 32. So if you importing a single land tile place 32 x 32 here.
7) Click the Import Picture check box.
8) Click on the top section of the land tile editor where you want your new land tile to reside. It will place a copy of your picture in the editor.
9) Click on the Import Picture check box again to return to edit mode -OR- repeat until you have all your pictures imported.
10) Fill out all the tile attribute and combat map data as needed.
11) After you have finished, you can save your land tile set and return to the Picture Editor and delete them from your scenario file. They are no longer needed as the actual graphics data is stored with the land tile set now.
If you want to work on all 200 tiles at once, see "Possible Shortcut for Large Jobs" below for a technique of saving yourself some serious effort.
Import Icon: Similar to importing pictures, you can import a color icon image for use as a land tile. Here is the step by step on how to do that.
1) Place your color icon into the file "Scenario" using ResEdit and remember the ID. For info on how to add color icons to your scenario files using ResEdit see the chapter "Adding Special Land Tiles"
2) Place the ID of the color icon in the field just below the words "Import Icon"
3) Click the "Import Icon" check box. All color icons are assumed to be 32x32 in size only and you need not fill in any Height and Width values as they are ignored.
4) Click on the Land Tiles where you want the color icon image to be placed.
5) If you have more icons you can increment to the next/previous ID with the +/- buttons. When finished, click the "Import Icon" check box again to turn it off and return to edit mode.
6) Save your land tile set.
7) You can now delete those color icons from your scenario files using ResEdit as you will no longer need those as the graphics data is now stored with the land tile data.
Possible Shortcut For Large Jobs
If by chance you want to work on the graphics for the entire land set all at once instead of one by one you can use the following technique.
1) Take a screen shot of the standard land set that comes closes to what you want to change -OR- set up a new graphic that is 640 pixels wide by 320 pixels tall in your graphics program of choice.
NOTE: You still need to have the note icon in any tile set so it is often easier to use a screen shot of a standard set as a basis to work with.
2) Make any changes to the graphics you see fit to make.
3) Convert the graphic to the standard Mac system palette. If you don't know what I am talking about here then odds are you're in over your head already and should stick with using the standard land tile sets.
4) Import the picture just like any other (See above for a step by step on that) and give it a height and width of 640 x 320 and place the picture in the upper left tile. WHAM! You just slapped all 200 custom icons on there in one shot.

sections.title: Spell Editor
sections.text:
29. Spell Editor
Top
Spell Editor
The ability to edit and use your own spells is new in version 5.1.2 This chapter will go over how to edit your own spells and any restrictions on their use.
To access the spell editor select "Scenario Data" from the land editor when you first launch Divinity. On the left side of the screen that appears will be a button "Edit Spells"
IMPORTANT
: Before you can edit custom spells you need to copy the file "Data Spell" into your scenario folder. A copy of that file is inside the folder "New Scenario" that came with the Divnity Update. If later you decide you don't want any custom spells you can just delete that file.
That will bring up a screen similar to that shown below.
First a brief rundown on what this is and what you can and can't do.
Spells are broken down into 5 categories. Only the last of which you can edit.
Sorcerer Spells Numbered from 1101 through 1715
Priest Spells Numbered from 2101 through 2715
Enchanter Spells Numbered from 3101 through 3715
Special Spells Numbered from 4101 through 4715
Custom Spells Numbered from 5101 through 5715
The data for the first four types of spells is kept in the Realmz Data Files" folder and the data for "Custom Spells", the ones you create, is kept in your scenario folder.
If you have a scenario started already you can update your scenario to include custom spells by dragging the file "Data Spell" from the Divinity 5.1.2 Updater into your scenario folder.
Lets run down what each field on the spell editor does.
_____________________________________________________
Fixed Range
: If the spell has a specific distance it can be cast in combat you can set the maximum range of the spell here. If you want the spell to require a direct line of site to the target, set the Fixed Range to a negative number.
Example
: A range of -12 would allow the caster to cast the spell up to 12 hexes away but would require that they have a clear line of site to the target as well.
Power Range
: If the spell can be cast further with increased power levels, place the number of hexes the range extends for each power level here.
Example
: If you want the spell to go 2 hexes plus 3 hexes per power level place a Fixed Range value of 2 and a Power Range value of 3. A power level 5 spell would have a range of 2 + 3x5 = 17
+ / - To Hit %
: This really applies only to spells that will be used to mimic missile weapons. As you may know already, missile weapon targeting and use is pretty much the same as just targeting a spell. If the spell you are creating will be used for something like a +8 Arrow of Destruction then you can place a +40 in this field to simulate a +8 weapon. Each + value of a magic weapon is equivalent to +5% to Hit.
+ / - To DRV %
: This will let you adjust the + or - to the "Damage Reduction Vs. Spell Type" If you want the spell to be harder or easier to resist you can adjust that by adding in a modifier here.
Example
: A mushroom plant may often blow spores in a characters face in an attempt to charm them. However, the spores do not work very often so they may have a -50% DRVs Charm to work.
No. of Attacks
: Some missile weapons may have multiple attacks per target. As an example, Throwing Stars are thrown 2 per target. By entering a value of 2 here you can cause the damage/effect of the missile weapon (Or spell) to take place twice.
Can Rotate
: If the spell is a Wall Spell such as "Wall of Flame" or some other spell that lets you rotate the spell to various orientations, check this box.
NOTE
: To make a spell rotate it must be a wall shaped spell. Enter a value of 3 as the Target Type and a value of 10 as the Spell Size.
+ / - To DRV / Level:
This is similar to + / - To DRV % except that the value here is multiplied by the power level of the spell. This will make the spell tougher to DRV for each power level of the spell.
Example
: You may have a charm spell that can only target one foe. However, for each power level of the spell, that target may have a -10% to DRV the spell. Thus making a higher power level spell tougher to resist.
+ / - To Resist / Level
: This is similar to + / - To DRV % except that the value here is multiplied by the power level of the spell and affect the targets ability to resist the spell outright. Some spells may still do damage even if the target is successful with a DRV Vs. Spell Type.
Example
: A fireball will still do 50% damage if a target DRVs the spell. However, if the target resists the spell outright it will take 0 damage. You can make the spell tougher to Resist by adding in a value here.
Resist Type
: There are 4 possible values you can enter here.
0 = Normal Spell. Target can resist or DRVs for half damage.
1 = No Resist. Target can't resist the spell but can still DRVs the spell to take half damage.
2 = No DRVs. Target can resist the spell outright but will not be capable of DRVs the spell to reduce the damage or effect.
3 = No Resist, No DRVs. This spell will always affect the target. In general this is often used for beneficial spells such as healing or protection spells. No target will resist a beneficial spell.
Base SP Cost
: The number of spell points it will take to cast this spell at power level 1. Each additional power level will require the same number of spell points.
NOTE
: If the spell is a special spell that will always be cast at power level 1 no matter the situation, you can prevent the player from selecting power levels higher than 1 by placing a negative value as a base power level. Example: Teleport Party is always cast as a power level 1 spell. The base cost is -50 which means it will cost 50 spell points to cast and can only be caste as a power level 1 spell.
Fixed Damage
: If the spell causes physical damage of any kind due to fire, cold, blades or just plain magical damage you can set the amount here. The left field is the low range and the right field is the high range. The spell will cause a random amount of damage from X to X regardless of the power level the spell is cast at.
Power Damage
: If the spell causes physical damage of any kind due to fire, cold, blades or just plain magical damage you can set the amount done per power level of the spell here. The left field is the low range and the right field is the high range. The spell will cause a random amount of damage from X to X regardless for each power level the spell is cast at.
NOTE
: Fixed Damage and Power Damage can be used in conjunction. You can have a spell that does from 1-20 points of fixed damage PLUS 1-5 points of damage for each power level as well.
Fixed Duration
: If the spell will have a lasting effect you can set the duration here. The left field is the low range (In combat rounds) and the right field is the high range (In combat Rounds). If the spell is cast in camp, each 5 minutes of game time is equivalent to 1 combat round for purposes of duration.
Power Duration
: If the spell will have a lasting effect you can set the duration here. The left field is the low range (In combat rounds) and the right field is the high range (In combat Rounds). If the spell is cast in camp, each 5 minutes of game time is equivalent to 1 combat round for purposes of duration.
This time is then multiplied by the number of power levels the spell was cast at.
NOTE
: Fixed Duration and Power Duration can be used in conjunction. You can have a spell that lasts from 1-4 rounds PLUS 1-2 rounds for each power level as well.
The next two values may seem like they would always be the same, and for the most part they almost always are.
Spell Class
: Each spell must fall into a category of spell for purposes of damage resolution, DRVs checking or creature immunities. If you can't think of any category for the spell then make it category 8.
Any spells that are defined as missile weapon spells such as arrows, darts or other missile weapons should be category 9.
Damage Type
: Each spell must fall into a category of spell for purposes of damage resolution, DRVs checking or creature immunities. If you can't think of any category for the spell then make it category 8.
Any spells that are defined as missile weapon spells such as arrows, darts or other missile weapons should be category 9.
Name
: Enter the name of the spell. Don't make it anything real fancy or long and don't use any special characters. Strictly letters and numbers.
Can Cast In Combat
: If this spell can be cast during the heat of battle then check this box. Some spells and effects may not be compatible with battle mode and should not be allowed to be cast in battle unless you are sure it is BATTLE SAFE.
Can Cast In Camp
: If this spell can be cast in camp then check this box. Some spells are usable only in a peaceful situation and may not be safe to cast in battle. Something like CHARM FOE should only be set to be cast in battle.
NOTE
: All spells will be available to be cast during a complex encounter resolution regardless of the Can Cast parameters of the spell.
Target Type
: Each spell must have a target type that governs how the spell can be used in either camp or combat. If the spell does not fall into any category that you can determine then select category 12 (Special)
-1 = Multi Open Space: This is a special target type that must be targeted on open terrain. The most common use for this target type is some type of summon spell. Since you cant summon creatures into solid material they must target an OPEN SPACE as a target.
0 = Multi Target: Any spell that can target multiple targets. Spells such as Fire Flies or Charm Foe can target multiple targets.
1 = Single Target: If the spell will only have a single target regardless of the spell size. Spells such as Fireball or Brimstones can only target one location.
2 = Not Used:
3 = Fixed Size: Some spells cover a set area regardless of the power level. These spells often do a larger amount of damage or last longer. To set just which fixed size you want, you can enter a value in SPELL SIZE or click on the "Spell Size" button until the size you wish appears.
4 = Area X Power: This spell type will increase the size of the spell as the power level of the spell goes up.
5 = Self: If the spell only affects the caster then use this type. Most potions should be of SELF type as he who drinks it is often the one that is effected.
6 = Ray: If the spell projects like a ray from the caster to the target. Spells like Psionic Spear or Scorched Earth are a couple of examples of this type of spell.
7 = Party: If the spell effects the party as a whole. Do not be confused into thinking this spell will just effect each member with some effect. This is to denote spells that affect the "Party Conditions" such as Water Breathing, Silent Sentry, Ogre Hide, Torches etc....
8 = Single Open Target: Similar to -1 except it allows only a single target.
9 = All Friendly: This spell will affect everybody who is friendly to the party at the time it is cast. If monsters cast this spell it will affect those that have the same "Traitor" value as that of the caster.
10 = All Enemies: This spell will affect everybody who is NOT friendly to the party at the time it is cast. If monsters cast this spell it will affect those that have a different "Traitor" value as that of the caster.
11 = Special: A generic spell type that does not really have a target. Spells like "Identify Objects" or "Speak Language" are examples of such spells.
Spell Size
: If the spell has a target type of 3 then you will have to specify a spell size. You can type a value here or click the "Spell Size" button to cycle through the different spell sizes.
Spell Effect
: This is where you specify any special effect a spell may have on the target. If the spell strictly does damage then you can leave this set to 0. If it does something special then click and hold the "Spell Effect" button and select from the popup menu to choose the special effect of the spell.
Spell Casting / Resolution Sounds
: This will determine the sound that is heard when the spell is cast and when it hits its target and effects are resolved.
Cast Icon
: Here you can set the icon that will be displayed when the spell is being targeted. This will also be the icon that is shown as it travels to the target.
Note: You now have access to additional visual effects for custom spells. In the spell editor you can now access 5 new special effects. These effects apply to the way the spell looks as it moves accross the screen.
You can access these new effects by typing a code of 20-24 in the "Cast Icon" field in the lower left hand corner of the spell editor.
I needed these for use with the high-tech weapons used in a portion of the Mithril Vault scenario. However, since it is there I figured I would tell you about them.
Type 20 = Lazer Beam
Type 21 = Scatter Laser Beams
Type 22 = Expanding Rings
Type 23 = Constricting Rings
Type 24 = Expanding & Closing Rings
Resolution Icon
: This is the icon that will be used to show the effect of the spell on the target.
Que. Icon
: Some spells have a lasting effect and stick around the battlefield for a number of combat rounds. If your spell will have a duration that allows it to cover an area of the battle field, select an icon that will be used to denote the affected area. If there is an icon selected in this field the game will assume it is a spell with a duration.
That pretty much covers what each field does. You can browse through and even copy the standard spells to your custom spells if you wish.
Special notes on some spells you may want to construct
:
Monster Summoning Spells
: If you want to create some type of monster summoning spell then enter a value of 58 in the special effect field.
To set the toughness of monsters to be summoned place a value from 1 (Weakest) to 7 (Strongest) in the
Spell Size
field.
Be sure to set "Spell Class" to 0 (Zero) if you want a random creatures. If you want to make the spell summon a specific monster every time then put the Monster ID in the "Spell Class" field. It is this way because I ran out of variable space so I had to sort of sneak it in there somehow.
Increase Attribute Spells
: If you want a spell that can increase a basic attribute of a character such as Brawn or Agility permanently then enter a value of 66 in teh special effects field. If you want the attribute that is to be increased to be random then leave the Spell Size field set to 0. Otherwise set it to the ID of the Attribute you want increased. (See Key-Codes Menu for ID Numbers).
To use it to increaes stamina, enter a value of 10 in Spell Size.
To use it to increaes spell points, enter a value of 11 in Spell Size.

sections.title: Race Editor
sections.text:
30. Race Editor
Top
Race Editor
You will not be able to edit any of the standard races, castes or spells. You can either copy them to a new record and tweak them to your liking or create new ones from the ground up.
To access the editors for race, caste or spell editing select "Scenario Data" from the main land edit screen when you first launch Divinity. You will see some new buttons. "Edit Races", "Edit Castes" and "Edit Spells"
IMPORTANT
: The first time you open the Race Editor it will create a new "Data Race" file inside your scenario folder. If later you decide you don't want to include and custom races, you can just delete that file.
Lets take a look at the basic race editing screen as shown below.
Lets go through each field and explain what it describes. Then we will go over any special considerations you may need for various fields.
Race Name
: Duh!
(3)
(25)
Attributes
Min
Max
Bonus / Penalty
This section lets you set the minimum and maximum attributes a particular race can have. It also lets you set any bonus/penalty the typical specimen of this race gets. In this example, Orcs tend to be pretty strong and hardy creatures but tend to be a bit muscle bound and stupid. Just being an orc is pretty unlucky so they tend not to have a good affinity for luck either.
Edit Conditions
Click this button in order to give your race any permanent condition. Orcs are not a special race and thus have no inherent magical properties. However, if your race had the natural ability to regenerate or something along that line this is where you can set that trait.
Special Ability Modifiers +/- %
Here you can set your races special abilities or lack thereof. In this case, Orcs are not particularly stealthy creatures so they get -5 to Sneak Attack. They also don't have much of an eye for detail so they get -10 to detecting secret areas and -5 to detecting traps. The orcs lack of flexibility and dexterity comes back to haunt them yet again as they get -5 to acrobatic acts and -10 to disarm traps and -5 to picking locks.
What do orcs do well? Crush meat, bone and tendon like so much soda crackers. This gives them a good chance to inflict a major wound as they learn to crack skulls from the time of birth.
+/- To Hit
Here you can set your races attitudes towards other types of creatures. Orcs don't have any particular weaknesses towards any other types of creatures but they do gain +1 to hit Magic Using creatures. Orcs have a general dislike for creatures that use magic and put that little extra effort in cuffing them a good one when the opportunity arises. They also have a particular liking to attacking animals of all kinds. Sure, small cuddly kittens are best but they like to inflict pain on just about anything that has 3 or more legs.
Bonus / Penalty For
DRVs Spell Class
If your race has a particular resistance or weakness to various types of magic you can specify it here. Here the orcs hardy nature helps them ward off anything dealing with the elements like heat and cold. However, their lack of a sizable brain case makes them easy to charm and not very resistant to magic. Now you know why they have a dislike to magic casters.
Miscellaneous
Can Regenerate
: Can this create regenerate? If not, place a value of 1 here. The current races are set up so everybody can regenerate except any race that has even a drop of Elven blood.
Base Movement Points
: Humans are base 12. Base your races movement compared to this. Even though they are somewhat short and squat, orcs can really get those little legs pumping and tend to stay at top speed till they drop dead.
Magic Resistance
: This is in %. Orcs are one the downside of this trait. Again, the lack of intellect makes it difficult for them to resist magic of almost any form.
Two Handed Weapon
: Large weapons of this nature tend to be only effective if the creature wielding it had either great size or great leverage. Hefting a great sword around is like arm wrestling. Would you want to arm wrestle an orc.... Didn't think so.
Missile Weapon
: Though they are not very nimble creatures they still gain a +5% with missile weapons. The short but powerful arms makes the pull of the drawstring almost effortless. This lets them hold the bow very steady and concentrate on the shot.
Base Attacks
: Each melee or magical attack takes 2 attack points. In this case, the orc gets only 1 attack to start so they get 2 attack points. If you wanted them to start out with 3 attacks every 2 rounds you would put a value of 3 here. If you wanted them to have 2 attacks per round then you would put a value of 4 here etc...
Don't go too hog wild here as you can also award bonus attacks based on caste.
Max Attacks Per Round
: This is a limiting factor on the number of attacks this race can have. Again, the limited flexibility and agility of orcs keeps them from attaining "Bruce Lee Speeds".
This limiting factor is applied regardless of caste. Some castes can have a maximum number of attacks of 6 per round. However, if they are an orc they will never get more than 4 regardless.
That pretty much finishes up the basic setup of your race. Now lets set the last details you need to set before your Race will be ready to live and die in the Realmz.
Along the left side of the screen you will notice five buttons. Lets talk about what each is for and show you how to go about setting up the values needed to complete your race.
Usable Items:
Will let you determine which categories of items your race can use. Lets take a look as
Orcs have no real restrictions as to the types of items they can use. There are about 48 categories of items. There is some room left over for new types in the future but for now we only have the 48.
As you can see above, Orcs can use every type of item known. Take a look at some of the other races and see how some of them are limited in the types of items they can use. This is mostly due to physical traits that keeps the race from using the type of item in question.
As an example: Pixies are far too small to use large bulky weapons and armor so they are restricted from using these types of items. They can't use whips either as there is too much danger to their wings from the snapping of the whip over the back. Keep these kind of things in mind when you fill out this section of your race. Think of the practicality of the item in conjunction with how your race looks physically.
Possible Castes:
Here you can set which castes your race can be. Orcs are limited to the more combative casts such as Fighters, Archers and Rogues. They do have a limited ability to use magic as both a priest or as a dabbler. However, the more advanced magical castes are beyond their ability.
Race Description:
This screen is also where you determine the general nature of your race. You can check all that apply to your race. Some items are restricted as to the nature of the user. As an example, the item "Sword of the Underworld" can only be used by the Goblinoid races. (Orcs, Goblins, Hob Goblins) Other items may only be usable by Neutral Races, Elvish Races etc.
Short Races
: Any race this is exceptionally small. Even though many orcs are short, they do vary in size greatly much like humans do. Thus they would not be considered a short race such as Dwarves, Pixies, Brownies etc.
Elvish
: Any race that has Elvish heritage is classified as Elvish. Half Elves are considered Elvish under this rule.
Half Breed
: Any races that consist of several blood lines such as Half Orcs or Half Elves etc.
Goblinoid
: These refer to any race with their original origins based on an ancient race of Ogre. All goblins, hob goblins and orcs are descendants of the Ogre and thus are considered Goblinoid in heritage.
Reptilian
: If your race is covered in scales or bony plates (Warts don't count. That would be Goblinoid!) then they are Reptilian.
Nether Worldly
: Creatures that stem from a different plane of existence or have a supernatural existence. Demons and Vampires are a few examples of this type of race.
Goodly, Neutral, Evil Races
: Note, your race does not need to be classed as any of the other traits but they must have one of these three traits. Keep in mind that some races that you might think of as EVIL are in fact Neutral. The same holds true for Goodly Races. Though they are generally good in nature, humans are considered neutral. Goodly races consist of races nearly the entire population is good in nature with only a very few exceptions. Evil races are just the reverse. The vast majority of the population is evil in nature but there are a few exceptions .
Race Relations:
Not currently implemented. Still working on this stuff but here is what it will be all about.
Certain races affect each other differently when placed in the same party.
Example
: Humans and Vampires are ancient adversaries as are Dwarves and Orcs. If your party contains both Orcs and Dwarves, they both may suffer somewhat in battle as they will always be looking over their shoulder keeping an eye on their so called friend.
In addition, some races may benefit other characters. As an example: Furfoots are generally look upon with favor by most other races and other races may fight better with a Furfoot in the party.
This like/dislike races have for one another is NOT an even two way street however. As an example, Humans have a real dislike for vampires but Vampires sort of like humans. If they are both in the party, Humans will suffer in battle whereas vampires may suffer no ill effects or could even benefit. Crazy huh!
Age Parameters:
As you may or may not know already, Realmz 1.0.5 now supports the Aging of your characters. See the Realmz game manual for more details on that subject and how it can affect your characters. I will stick to how to go about setting up the parameters so your race ages gracefully.
Each race is separated into five age groups. To make it all easier to understand I will talk about it in terms of the HUMAN race as most of those reading this are human.
Youth
: This is when most characters start to adventure in life. The world seems like a large place but you intend to see it all.
Young
: This is a short period of life when your hormones are in full swing. Your sure of yourself in all maters.
Prime
: Your body is in the best shape of your life but will soon start to decay. On the good side of things the hormones have stopped clouding your judgment and you start to see the world for what it is. A dangerous and wonderful place.
Adult
: Middle age crisis has hit and physically you are feeling those aches and pains. You realize there is more to life than getting into bar brawls and you start to pursue the finder things in life.
Senior
: Though your body has failed long ago your mind has finally come into it's prime. You may not be able to outrun your enemies but you can surely outthink them.
Max Age
: Note that your characters will never really die. However, we need to set a max age that is realistic in order for characters to progress through the various stages of life. Also, once a character goes beyond the age specified by Max Age they receive less victory points.
When you fill in Max Age the ranges for the various stages are automatically calculated. If you later want to tweak those age group limits to your own liking you may.
When you create a character they may start in any particular age group depending on the caste they choose to follow. Fighters for example start out as a Youth where a Cabalist starts out in his prime. Each time a character ages to the point that they pass into a new age group, their stats. are modified as dictated by the column they just graduated into.
Example
:
1) A new human fighter has all their statistics generated.
2) All race and caste bonus/penalties are applied.
3) All bonus/penalties are applied according to their age group. In this case the YOUTH age group stats would get applied.
4) All race and caste minimum and maximums are check and stats adjusted accordingly.
As this human fighter ages and hits the ripe old age of 18 all the stats in the second column (Young) are applied.
Note that previous stats are NOT subtracted. All changes are cumulative and should balance out over the course of a lifetime. If you add up the bonus/penalty for any state across the board they will (And should) add up to zero. This reflect how traits come and go depending on age and is NOT used to award some races an overall bonus/penalty. Do that in the main race editing screen.
Choose New Set
: This is the last step in setting up your new race. For technical reason I wont go into there is a limited number of portraits that Realmz can use to depict characters. Right now Realmz is maxed out and that is why I only allow 6 basic portraits for each race.
Because of that you have to choose a set (Group of 6) from the current portraits to represent your race. I would love it if this limitation was not there but it is. At least until I figure out a way to get around it or apple changes the way the handle menu icons.
Click and hold the Choose New Set button to bring up a list of icon sets to choose from. Just select the set that closes represents your race. These will be used as the DEFAULT choices for a character during character generation. They will still be able to choose from any of the 100+ portraits available however.
Special Things To Consider:
Turning Undead
: In the section where you can set your races ability to turn undead. Do not place any negative values here. This trait should be either 0 or a positive value. Any positive value will give your race the ability to turn undead regardless of the caste they choose. This should be reserved for very special races that have a natural ability to turn undead. i.e. Vampires ARE undead so they have a natural ability to turn undead. Pixies also have a magical ability to turn undead as they are the purest of goodly creatures.
Max Age
: Don't set this too high or too low or characters will not progress through the stages in any kind of a realistic manner.
BAMN!
Done. You have a new race and when you go to generate a new character in Realmz this new race should be available to choose from. They will only be available in YOUR scenario as the information is stored within your scenario.

sections.title: Caste Editor
sections.text:
31. Caste Editor
Top
Editing Castes
To access the editor for castes select "Scenario Data" from the main land edit screen when you first launch Divinity. Select "Edit Castes"
There is quite a bit of info you need to specify for a new caste but it's all pretty easy to understand.
IMPORTANT
: The first time you open the Caste Editor it will create a new "Data Caste" file inside your scenario folder. If later you decide you don't want to include and custom castes, you can just delete that file.
Lets take a look at the basic caste editing screen as shown below.
For this example we will take a look at your basic Monk. First I will step through each field on the main edit screen and describe what each field represents.
Spell Casting
:
Sorcerer
: Check this box if this caste will be able to caste sorcerer spells.
Start
: The level the character must reach before they can access spell casting.
Max
: Maximum spell level available to the character.
Example
: If you check sorcerer and then place a value of 5 in start and 4 in max. That character would be able to cast up to 4th level sorcerer spells once they reach skill level 5.
Priest
: Same as sorcerer. A caste can only cast one type of spells. DO NOT select more than one type of spells to be cast by a character.
Enchanter: Same as sorcerer. A caste can only cast one type of spells. DO NOT select more than one type of spells to be cast by a character.
Caste Name
: Name of your caste.
Edit Conditions: If your caste starts with or gains special conditions you can edit those here. When you click on the "Conditions" button you will see the following dialog.
To give a caste a condition to start with, just place a 1 in any condition. That means any character level 1 or higher will have that condition. In this example, the monk will get Regeneration when they reach level 20, Protection from Chemicals at level 10 and Protection from Mental attacks when they reach level 5.
Can Use Missile Weapons
: If the cast is capable of using missile weapons such as bows, darts etc... check this box.
Missile Bonus Damage
: Some castes receive extra damage when using missile weapons. This damage is equivalent to a random amount from 1 to Character Level. This should apply to any castes that specialize in missile weapon attacks such as archers or marksman.
Special Note On Attributes
: In both the race and caste editor you will see fields where you can set a minimum, maximum, bonus or penalty to attributes. All of these apply to each new character.
Attributes
:
Min: The minimum value this caste can have for any particular attribute.
Max: The maximum value this caste can have for any particular attribute.
Penalty / Bonus: Some castes may receive a bonus or penalty to some attributes. In the example of a Monk they gain +1 to judgment, +2 to Agility and +1 to Vitality.
When a character is generated a random value from 1 to 18 is generated for each attribute. Any bonus or penalty is then added.
Special Ability
:
Each caste has a number of possible special abilities. Each caste has a specific starting value and an amount that they can gain when they level up.
If you leave a value blank for starting and level up then that special ability is not available to that particular caste.
Special Note On Turning Undead
: In the section where you can set your castes ability to turn undead. Do not place any negative values here. This trait should be either 0 or a positive value. Any positive value will give your caste the ability to turn undead regardless of the race they choose.
Stamina
: Starting stamina your caste will receive. Stamina = random amount from 1 to X. Lvl Up: Caste will get random amount from 1 to X for each skill level beyond the first.
Strength Damage Bonus
: Some castes gain a bonus to damage and the ToHit statistic when they have high strengths. Your caste will gain +1 to damage and +5 ToHit for each point of strength over this value. MAX: They gain this + to Damage and ToHit for each point of strength up to a maximum strength value of X.
Above Example
: Monks gain +1 to Damage and +5 ToHit for each point of strength over 15 to a maximum strength of 25.
Dodge Missile
: The ability to dodge missile is calculated on a character agility. However, some castes may gain an initial bonus to dodge and can improve this skill when they level up.
Melee ToHit
: This is the statistic that controls how easy your caste can hit an opponent during battle with Melee (Non missile) weapons. You can set the initial ToHit % as well as the amount they gain for each level beyond the first.
Hand To Hand
: Every caste has the ability to do some damage with bare hands. (Feeble as it may be for some.....) However, some are what we call in the biz... Lethal Weapons
Above Example
: Monks do normal 1-2 points of bare hand damage but gain 1-2 points of damage for each level they gain. A 20th level monk can do up to 40 points of damage with his bare hands. OUCH!
DRVs Spell Class
: Each caste may be more or less resistant to some types of magic or damage. The base for these statistics is based on many factors such as race, age etc... However, you can set any bonus or penalty your caste may receive here.
Caste Category
: Each caste must be part of a larger main group of castes. You must set your caste under one of the 7 main groups. Look under the key-codes menu to determine the ID of your parent caste group and place it here.
Minimum Age Group
: If your caste is a highly specialized caste that may take years of training to master then you should set the minimum age group higher. There are 5 age groups. 1 being the youngest and 5 being the oldest. For most magical castes you should start your character as a 2 or 3 to adjust for the years of learning one must do as an apprentice. Other castes such as fighters can pretty much be started as soon as one is strong enough to pick up a stick and should start them out as group 1 (Youth)
+ / - Movement Points
: Some castes may be quicker on their feet than others. This may be due to special training but may also be due to the type of clothing worn. Most magical classes wear robes with pockets full of reagents. Not something you can exactly run around in.
Magic Resistance
: This value is a multiplier. Enter only a whole number such as 1, 2 or 3. Do not use any decimals such as 1.5
Each character has a magic resistance that is based on many factors such as race, knowledge and judgment. However, some castes can have this multiplied. In general, the more skill a caste is in magic the higher this multiplier should be. A value of 1, 2 or 3 should pretty much cover most castes. Anything higher than 3 is getting out of line.
Two Handed Weapon
: A % modifier applied to the ToHit statistic to represent a castes ability to use two handed weapons such as huge swords, staves etc..
Above Example
: The monk is somewhat skilled with using weapons requiring two hands such as staves and gains a +5% ToHit with such weapons.
Max Stamina Bonus
: All castes gain extra stamina for having a Vitality score over 15. However, some castes are limited as to the amount of bonus they can get. In general the more hardy the caste is the higher this bonus should go. However, some may be limited to +1 or +2 bonus if they are of a more delicate nature. (Sorry warlocks.... Pump some more iron)
Bonus Attacks
: The number of attacks a caste starts with in addition to the normal 1 attack per round. These are added as 1/2 attacks per round. A value of 1 here would mean the caste would start with 1 and 1/2 attacks per round. Remember that if a character has 1/2 attack left at the end of the round it is carried over to become a full attack the following round.
Example
: If you enter a value of 1 here that caste would start with 1.5 attacks per round. Meaning on round 1 they get 1 attack. Round 2 they get 2 attacks. Round 3 they get 1 attack. Round 4 they get 2 attacks etc..
If you enter a value of 2 here they get a full attack bonus to start. That would give them 2 attacks per round to start with.
Max Attacks Per Round
: Each caste has a maximum number of attacks they can achieve during combat. The most you should allow for any caste is 6 attacks.
Max Spells Per Round
: The maximum number of spells a caste can cast during a combat round. Most non castes that can caste spells but are also good at normal combat should be limited to 1 spell per round. Only those castes that really concentrate on magic should be allowed more spells per round. Don't go too hog crazy here as it would be easy picking for a pack of warlocks if they could each caste 10 spells the first round.
Special Note On Castes
: Though you can't change any of the basic castes you can view them. Look them over to see how I have things set and try to learn by example. Don't be tempted to make some type of super caste as it will spoil the game. A good caste has to have a balance of good and bad points. If you give them great combat skills, then limit them on some front. Either by giving them lower maximum attributes or make them vulnerable to magic or whatever. Every body has an Achilles heal.
Victory Points
: When you edit victory points you can set the required number of victory points to achieve any particular skill level. Each value is what is required to achieve the next skill level.
Example
:
Level 1: 3,000
Level 2: 6,000
Level 3: 12,000
Level 4: 25,000
Some may view this as needing only 25,000 points to achieve level 4 but that is not the case. To achieve level 1 you need 3,000. Then to get to level 2 you need another 6,000. To get to level 3 you need another 12,000 and to get to level 4 you need another 25,000. That would be a total of 46,000 to get to level 4.
Attacks
: Here you can set the skill level at which your castes gains 1/2 attacks.
Example
:
In this example, the character would gain 1/2 attack at level 4. Another 1/2 attack at level 7. Levels 11, 14, 19, 23, 27 and 31 would also gain them 1/2 attack.
If the character begins with bonus attacks or gains bonus attacks due to racial heritage then the character would still gain bonus attacks at these levels.
Note however, that the character may be limited to a maximum number of attacks due to a caste or racial restriction. If that is the case they will not gain more attacks per round than is specified by the race or caste definition.
Usable Items
:
Each caste is capable of using a set group of items. If your caste is capable of using items of a specific category just check those that they can use. It is quick to see which items a Monk can and can't use by the above example.
Use a little logic here when selecting which items your caste can or can't use. Just like pixies are not about to use a whip (Might get tangled with their wings) a monk is not likely to use plate armor or a huge kite shield.
Initial Items / Gold
:
Each caste should start out with some basic equipment usable by that character. This is not required but on average almost anybody would set off with at least something. Any equipment you select your character to have will be worn by them to start with if they can.
Items will be attempted to be worn in order from the top down. So if you give them 5 melee weapons, the one nearest the top of the list will be worn first.
That pretty much covers the basics of creating your own castes for use in your scenario.

sections.title: Text Import • Export • Spell Checking
sections.text:
32. Text Import • Export • Spell Checking
Top
You want to run all the strings in your scenario through a spell checker but your not sure how.
Here is a step by step process on how you can do that.
1)
Make a backup of your scenario just in case something goes haywire. This feature is new and it may do some unpredictable things. Don't chance it.
2)
Load your scenario and click the button "Strings" on the main land editing screen that comes up when you launch Divinity.
3)
At the bottom of this screen you will see 3 new buttons.
- Export Text To File "Export Text": When you click this it will create a file in your Realmz folder by the name of "Export Text" It will overwrite any file already there by the same name without notifying you.
In that file it will place all your strings one after the other separated by a marker tag that should look like this: "  " That's just he apple symbol with 20 blank spaces in front and back of it.
Depending on the word processor you use to do your spell checking that apple symbol may or may not show up as an apple at all. It may look like some Greek letter or just a box like  because the font in your word processor does not have the  defined. No matter, the effect is the same and you should not modify it in any way.
You must NOT remove any of the  symbols for ANY reason. If you remove so much as even one then all your strings will be shifted when imported and your scenario text will not work correctly.
REPEAT!!!!!!!!!!!!! DO NOT REMOVE ANY OF THOSE  TAGS WHILE SPELL CHECKING. THEY ARE THERE SO DIVINITY CAN IMPORT YOUR STRINGS AND PLACE THEM WITH THE SAME ID AS BEFORE. IF YOUR NOT SURE ABOUT SOME STRANGE LOOKING SYMBOL IN THE TEXT FILE DURING SPELL CHECKING JUST LEAVE IT THERE, ODDS ARE IT BELONGS THERE.
4)
Once you have created the "Export Text" file open it up with whatever word processor you want to use. It's a plain text file and you should open it up as such. Don't attempt to open it as any type of formatted text. Just PLAIN TEXT.
5)
Spell check your document. Do not go hog wild by replacing whole sections of text with different text as the maximum string length for each string is 255. If you add too much text then when imported it will delete part of your text or may even screw the whole thing up. Wait till you import the text back into Divinity before you edit large blocks of text.
6)
When your done spell checking, save your document as "Text Only" Again, this is the format it was in when you opened it and has to be the format when you save it. If you save it as a Microsoft Word document or as Claris Works or as anything other than "Plain Text" you are wasting your time as it will not import at all. Be sure to save it to the same location as where it loaded from i.e. The Realmz folder as that is where Divinity will expect it to be when it imports the text.
7)
Again, load your scenario and click "Strings" to bring up the string editing window. Now click the button "Import Text From "Export Text" File
And Rename To "Data SD2"'"
That will convert all your strings back into the proper form and save the data in a file called "Data SD2" inside your Realmz folder. You can then move the file "Data SD2" into your scenario folder and replace the one that is there already. You should then check to see if the strings imported correctly by viewing your strings in the string editor.
8)
Lastly, you will want to clean up any text overrun. When you spell check your strings you may have extended the length of some of them past the 255 character limit. If so, then some text may be cut off from the end. To search for strings that may have fallen prey to this problem:
a) Open the string editor.
b) Move to string ID 0 (Zero).
c) Click the button "Find Next Maximum Length String.
Use This To Clean Up Possible Errors After Importing Text From Spell Checker".
This will find the first string that uses all 255 characters. If it ends as it should then no problem, click the button again to move to the next one. However, if you notice that the last word is partially gone then you need to edit the text to be a tad shorter as it has overrun the 255 character limit.
That's it. Sounds complicated and in a way it is. Such is the world. Should save you a lot of grief when it comes to spell checking though.

sections.title: Scenario Security • Registration Codes
sections.text:
33. Scenario Security • Registration Codes
Top
Scenario Security & Registration Codes
If you do not enter any kind of Registration Codes for your scenario, anybody who downloads it will be able to play the entire scenario.
To install a Registration Code into your scenario you need to do a few simple things.
Click "Scenario Data" from the Land Editor. That will bring up the following screen.
Figure 22.0
In the fields Code Segment 1 and Code Segment 2, enter any sequence of characters up to 20 characters long.
Once you have entered these codes, they will be coded into the scenario file. They can't be changed once entered and they can't be retrieved by anybody. INCLUDING YOU! DO NOT LOSE THEM. Write them down in a safe place as there is no way for you to ever find them again from the scenario files once they are encoded. If you protect it and then lose these codes, you are out of luck.
Either make them something you can remember or have them tattooed on your wrist.
Now that you have chosen your Code Segments you need to place this information into the Divinity Decoder™
Run Divinity Decoder and you will see a screen like the one below.
Figure 22.1
Divinity Decoder can store registration information for up to 6 scenarios you have created at a time.
Place the EXACT TITLE of your scenario in one of the Title fields. Below that place your secret Code Segments in the fields provided.
When a person sends you the required registration fee, they will need to supply you with their Name and the Serial Number of their copy of Realmz. Place the name and serial number in the fields at the top left of the screen.
The code that will allow them to pass your registration security will appear in the upper right hand corner. That is the number you need to send back along with the EXACT NAME you used to generate the code so they can play the full version.
It is best to avoid special characters in the name. Try and stick with the standard English alphabet and avoid any extra spaces.
Where to put your security in your scenario
You have your code segments installed and you know how to generate a code to give to registered users. All you need to do now it place a roadblock in your scenario that requires people to register it in order to play the whole thing.
Your best bet is to create some type of choke point that separates the free portion from the pay to play portion. The best way is to separate the two sections by an action point. The only way to the second portion is by walking past this action point. Then place a CODE 99 on this Action Point. Whenever a code 99 is encountered it will require the player to enter the valid registration info you provided in order to pass.
Upon completion of the registration, it's best to deactivate the registration action point so they are not tormented with it over and over.
Added Security
: In addition to using the code 99 to create a roadblock you can also use a CODE 98 in locations to check that the scenario has been registered. This helps prevent people from editing the saved game file to place the party beyond the registration point.
The best way to use this is to cover an entire land level that is in the pay to play section with a Random Rectangle. Set that rectangle to activate an X-AP every now and then. In that X-AP you have a code 98 that will test to see if the scenario is registered. If not it will quit the game. This pretty much lets you constantly test to see if the person has paid and bail out as soon as it detects that they have not paid but somehow got beyond the registration point.

sections.title: Things to check before you release your sceanrio
sections.text:
34. Things to check before you release your sceanrio
Top
Things to check before you release your scenario.
Here are some things you will want to make sure you check before you release your scenario.
1)
Make a copy of your scenario and place it on some floppies. Can't stress this enough. Don't trust that hard drive with your only copy.
2)
Make sure all your monsters have the appropriate icons. Because of all the possibilities of changing the icon sets for monster icons, make sure that each monster has the correct icon set.
3)
Click on "Create Sets" in the monster editor. This will copy all the data from your normal monster set into the Monster Monsters and Mega Monsters. It will also increase the strenght of each monster by a certain amount for each set.
4) Trim the fat!
In the course of making a scenario you often end up creating levels and encounters that are no longer used in the final product. You can reduce the size of your scenario files by trimming off any excess file data you don't need.
To do this, click "Trim the Fat" from the Scenario Data screen. This will bring up a list of the various files that hold your data. If you know for a fact that you only have 5 land levels, then enter a 5 in the field "Last Land Level" and check the "Trim This File" box. When you click DO IT all files with the "Trim This File" box checked will be chopped off at the point you indicate. This can greatly reduce the size of your scenario files if you have excess data.
Be careful though as once this info is deleted, it can't be retrieved.
5) Set Starting Parameters
Make sure you starting position, and recomended levels is correct.

sections.title: Realmz for Win95/98/NT4
sections.text:
35. Realmz for Win95/98/NT4
Top
Realmz for Windows 95/98/NT4
Realmz 7.0 is the first version that is compatible with Windows. However, at this time Divinity is not. In order to create and edit your scenario’s you still need to use a Mac. However, people who play Realmz on windows are still capable of playing scenarios you create.
Before they can play them they must be converted into Windows format. To convert your scenario into a format playable on Windows follow the below step by step instructions.
1) Locate and run the utility program "Split File.bin"
2) Drag a copy of your scenario (Mac version) over the Split File window.
3) A folder by the name of "Transfer" will be created on your main hard drive. Inside will be another folder that contains a Windows compatible version of your scenario.
NOTE: If you plan on posting this to a web site for windows users to use you will most likely need to compact it. However, the vast majority of windows users DO NOT own a copy of Aladdin Stuffit Expander for windows. Even though it exists, most windows users still use some form of WinZip for opening archives. As such, you may want to locate a copy of MacZip which will allow you to compact your Windows version of your scenario into a .zip file.
OR- make it plain to those that download your scenario that they need to get a copy of Aladdin Expander for Windows. If you click the "Links" button on the main Fantasoft web site you will see where you can download a copy of Aladdin Expander for Windows.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text:
36. Frequently Asked Questions
Top
Frequently Asked Questions
